title: Lorenzo Tio's clarinet tone, compared to Benny Goodman
summary: Gorman describes Tio's clean, medium-volume tone and how he stood while teaching.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Well, I was going to ask a little bit more about T.O., what style, since he isn't living, I never got to hear him except the records he made with Pirone, but how did he play? What was his tone like and what style did he have? Can you tell us something?

Well, Pirone, not Pirone, T.O., T.O., he fella had a really very nice tone. He had a really clarinet tone. His clarinet was on the order of, like, say, it was very little different between him and Benny Goodman. And you know Benny Goodman is a clarinet man.
Did he have an extra loud tone or a clearer tone? What did you say?
He wasn't a loud man, but he was what you call a really, he's in between.
Played nice and clean like Benny Goodman you mean?
Clean, that's right. And what he made was that. Yeah. Was just as clean, clean. He wasn't a rough fella, you know, you got clarinet plays rough.

When he had bladder, bladder, I know that it's so, sometimes he knocks it out of tone, you know what I mean? But he wasn't a guy like that. Guess what he would make? It was that. And I used to admire him all the time by him to teach me. See, because sometimes I'd be in the front and he's a man when he's teaching you, he'd never sit down by you. He'd stand up and see how you'd make up. Then he'd walk in the back. Then he'd stop and say, no, that's going to go on.
